consistency_checks.detail: All severity ≥3 findings (diastolic BP, PDW, low CO₂, HbA1c, systolic BP) are addressed by at least one diagnosis in the differential.
Primary hyperaldosteronism and essential hypertension probabilities were mis‑aligned with the evidence; fibromuscular dysplasia was under‑weighted.
Serum potassium, renin/aldosterone, creatinine/eGFR, urine ACR, BMI, and lipid panel are absent, limiting verification of several diagnoses.

top_concerns: Over‑estimation of primary hyperaldosteronism without electrolyte or hormonal data
Under‑estimation of fibromuscular dysplasia despite classic demographic
Inclusion of low‑probability autoimmune diagnoses with insufficient supporting evidence
Absence of essential renal function and metabolic labs (K⁺, creatinine, eGFR, urine studies)
Lack of objective obesity/metabolic syndrome metrics (BMI, lipids)
review_summary: The junior differential captured most relevant categories but mis‑weighted the top diagnoses and omitted key secondary causes such as fibromuscular dysplasia. Several high‑severity lab abnormalities (elevated PDW, low CO₂) are not adequately explained by the higher‑probability entries. Adjusted probabilities reflect a stronger role for essential hypertension and fibromuscular dysplasia, with reduced emphasis on hyperaldosteronism and autoimmune etiologies. Additional targeted labs and imaging are required to confirm or exclude the secondary causes.
